parts.text:
Call the Skill tool with "grilling".

Relative paths in this skill (e.g., scripts/, references/) are relative to this base directory.

Create a dashboard for visualizsation of the customer feedback anaalysis, competitor research, and trend research. This dashboard is aimed to be a business intelligence dashboard. You can suggest better design if you find better UI/UX than my proposal. The user of this dashboard is a Product Manager for car at BMW. 

My design idea: 
Overall layout: Dashboard with navigation on the left, main content middle with breadcrumbs on top, and collapsible chat window (or popup) on the right side
Analysis page: A selection of cars with some categorization based on series (G or F series). See: [Image 1] . When a user click on a car, the car page will be shown.
Car Page: Contain a car page showing analysis of all data based on each regions. USer can choose region via a dropdown (world or certain country). I am open for visualitzation option and suggestion but it should show prioritization of aspects of car that need should be improved, complete with all the reasoning and supporting data citation. From the first view of the car page, the user should be able to see the overall incentives for the car and incentives for each aspect. See: [Image 2]
The user wants me to invoke the grilling skill, so I should call the Skill tool to load its instructions before proceeding.

<skill_content name="grilling">
# Skill: grilling

Interview the user relentlessly until you reach a shared understanding. Map this as a **design tree**: every decision branches into the decisions that hang off it.

Work the tree in **rounds**. The **frontier** is every decision whose prerequisites are already settled: the questions you can ask _now_ without guessing at answers you haven't heard yet. Ask the whole frontier in one round: number each question and give your recommended answer. Then wait for the user's answers before the next round.

Format a round like so:

```
❓ **Q1** - **<question title>**: <question body, might be multiple paragraphs, including multiple choices>

➡️ <your recommended answer>

---

❓ **Q2** - **<question title>**: <question body, might be multiple paragraphs, including multiple choices>

➡️ <your recommended answer>
```

Each round the user answers reshapes the tree: settled decisions push the frontier outward and unblock questions that depended on them. Recompute the frontier and ask the next round. A question whose answer depends on another question still open in this round belongs to a _later_ round, not this one.

Finding _facts_ is your job, never the user's. When a frontier question needs a fact from the environment (filesystem, tools, etc.), dispatch a sub-agent to find it; don't ask the user for anything you could look up yourself. Don't block on it: a running exploration is an unsettled prerequisite, so only the questions downstream of it wait for the sub-agent to report; ask the rest of the frontier now. The _decisions_ are the user's: put each to them and wait.

The session is done when the frontier is empty: every branch of the design tree visited, nothing left silently assumed. Do not act on it until the user confirms you have reached a shared understanding.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/itsmeyaw/.claude/skills/grilling
Relative paths in this skill (e.g., scripts/, reference/) are relative to this base directory.
Note: file list is sampled.

</skill_files>
</skill_content>

The repo is an untouched Create Next App starter plus a feedback preprocessing pipeline. None of these exist yet: shadcn/ui, sidebar, breadcrumb, charts, chat, auth, API routes, or any competitor or trend research data. You're on branch `main`.

## 1. CONTEXT.md and docs
**`/Users/itsmeyaw/projects/bmwow/CONTEXT.md`** describes the domain as "BMW Customer Feedback". It is broken into aspects so product owners can see what owners praise, struggle with, want or report as broken, per model and engine type. Full term list:

- **Feedback:** one customer's comment about one vehicle, identified by its Feedback Explorer ID. Counts once however many aspects it has. (Avoid: row, record, review, entry)
- **Verbatim:** the customer's own text, exactly as written. (Avoid: comment, raw text, translated feedback)
- **Source:** the channel a feedback came in through (Source A–D). What each one means isn't confirmed. (Avoid: origin, provider)
- **Derivate:** the model code, e.g. F70, G60, G70. (Avoid: model, series, e-code)
- **Sales Description:** the marketing name, e.g. "BMW 1 Series". (Avoid: model name, product)
- **Engine Type:** ICE, PHEV or BEV. "BEVE" means BEV. (Avoid: powertrain, fuel type)
- **Aspect:** one thing a feedback says about one part of the vehicle. A feedback has zero or more, each with its own feedback type, buckets and sentiment. (Avoid: topic, tag, label, mention)
- **Feedback Type:** the source system's own class for an aspect: Likes, Difficult to Use, Wants or Defect. It belongs to the aspect, so one feedback can be both Likes and Defect.
- **VFC Label:** a human-assigned class from BMW's VFC taxonomy, made of an aspect term plus an aspect label.
- **Aspect Term:** VFC level 2, the component or feature, e.g. "Touch screen, operation".
- **Aspect Label:** VFC level 3, what was said about it, e.g. "Not user-friendly".
- **Unlabelled Feedback:** no usable VFC label (blank or "no_class_found"), so its aspects can only be inferred.
- **VFC Category:** one of 16 coarse buckets for aspect terms, e.g. "Infotainment & Connectivity".
- **Issue Type:** one of 11 coarse buckets for aspect labels, e.g. Malfunction, Usability Difficulty, Feature Request, Praise.
- **Unclassified:** a real bucket value, not a missing label. (Avoid: other, misc, unknown)
- **Taxonomy Mapping:** the reviewed list mapping every aspect term to a VFC category and every aspect label to an issue type.
- **Curated Aspect:** comes from a human VFC label.
- **Inferred Aspect:** extracted by an LLM from an unlabelled verbatim, limited to the same buckets.
- **Quote:** the exact passage supporting an inferred aspect. Curated aspects have none.
- **Sentiment:** Positive, Negative or Neutral, decided only by issue type. Praise is Positive; Feature Request and Unclassified are Neutral; everything else is Negative.
- **Intensity:** how strongly the customer says it, 0 to 1.
- **Sentiment Score:** intensity signed by sentiment, −1 to +1, always 0 for Neutral. It ranks aspects within a sentiment and never decides the sentiment.

**Other docs:**
- **`/Users/itsmeyaw/projects/bmwow/docs/preprocess-pipeline-spec.md`** is the full pipeline spec (status ready-for-agent). It lists 42 user stories for dashboard, search/RAG, operator and data-quality users. The Next.js dashboard and search UI are explicitly out of scope. Other points:
  - Search is meant to be hybrid, combining vector and text search with RRF fusion ("~15 lines in the app").
  - There is no date column in the source data, so time-series charts are impossible and dates must not be faked.
- **`/Users/itsmeyaw/projects/bmwow/AGENTS.md`** points to CONTEXT.md and adds the Next.js agent rules.
- **`/Users/itsmeyaw/projects/bmwow/README.md`** is the Create Next App default.
- There are no ADRs and no `adr/` directory.

## 2. Tech stack (`/Users/itsmeyaw/projects/bmwow/package.json`)
- **Framework:** next 16.4.0, react and react-dom 19.3.0, TypeScript 5. The package manager is pnpm 11.21.0.
- **Next config** (`/Users/itsmeyaw/projects/bmwow/next.config.ts`): `cacheComponents: true`, `partialPrefetching: true`, `experimental.agentFeedback`, and Turbopack with the `@tailwindcss/turbopack` loader.
- **Styling:** Tailwind v4. `/Users/itsmeyaw/projects/bmwow/src/app/globals.css` has only the default `@import "tailwindcss"` plus background/foreground variables.
- **Data:**
  - Database: `drizzle-orm` 1.0.0-rc.4, `drizzle-kit` (dev, not wired up, no `drizzle.config`), `pg`.
  - Other: `@libsql/client` (a leftover the spec calls "wrong database"), `csv-parse`, `dotenv`, `zod` ^4.6.5.
- **AI:** `openai` ^7.31.0 only. There is no Vercel AI SDK (`ai`, `@ai-sdk/*`).
- **Not installed:**
  - UI: no `components.json` (no shadcn/ui), no Radix, no lucide.
  - Charts: no recharts or any other chart library.
  - Auth: no auth library.
- **Tooling:** oxlint and oxfmt (`/Users/itsmeyaw/projects/bmwow/.oxlintrc.json`, `/Users/itsmeyaw/projects/bmwow/.oxfmtrc.json`), tsx, react-grab (dev).
- **MCP:** `/Users/itsmeyaw/projects/bmwow/.mcp.json` points at the Neon MCP server (`https://mcp.neon.tech/mcp`).
- **`/Users/itsmeyaw/projects/bmwow/.env`** holds `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `DATABASE_URL` (Neon project `bmwow`, PG 18, aws-us-east-2, per the spec).

## 3. App structure

## 4. Data layer
**Raw input:** `/Users/itsmeyaw/projects/bmwow/data/feedbacks/f70_feedback.csv`, `g60_feedback.csv` and `g70_feedback.csv`.
- Columns: `ID, Source, Brand, Sales Description, Country, Derivate (e-code), Engine Type, Feedback Type, Customer Feedback, Vfc level2 3 Name, Vfc level2 Name, Vfc level3 Name`.

**Pipeline:** `/Users/itsmeyaw/projects/bmwow/scripts/preprocess.ts` (563 lines, run with `pnpm preprocess`, flags `--limit N` and `--self-check`).
- Steps: read the CSVs, clean them (BEVE→BEV, strip brackets, trim), and deduplicate on ID.

There is no db client module (no `src/db/index.ts`).
- **`feedback_entries`:** `id`, `feedback_explorer_id` (unique), `source`, `brand`, `sales_description`, `country`, `derivate_code`, `engine_type`, `raw_feedback`, `embedding` vector(1536) with an HNSW index, `search_tsv` (generated tsvector with a GIN index), `created_at`.

parts.text:
The database is mostly populated now, so I'm moving into round one of open questions: where competitor and trend data would even come from since no source exists, what "incentives" should mean, how to model regions given a country-only, US-dominant dataset with a World/country dropdown and sample thresholds, and how to group the car catalog by derivative letter given the F70/G60/G70 pattern with no F60.

I'm also noting that F/G codes are BMW generation codes, so that list should stay data-driven from the DB. Beyond that: should chat be RAG over feedback with citations or just a UI shell, auth is a placeholder for now, engine type should probably be a second filter dimension on the car page, the UI stack should use shadcn with sidebar/breadcrumb/recharts in a dark BMW-styled theme, and car imagery still needs sourcing. The prioritization formula and visualization layout both hinge on how Q1 and Q2 get resolved, so I'm deferring those. For Q1 specifically, I'm leaning toward creating a research_findings table (competitor/trend, derivate, country, category, claim, source URL/title, published date) fed by a separate web-search research pipeline, though I need to clarify whether that research is handled by someone else before committing to this approach.

For Q2, I'd define a "Priority Score" per VFC category combining volume share and mean negative intensity, with overall car health as net sentiment, acknowledging there's no time-series data for trends. I'd default the prioritization unit to VFC category with drill-down into aspect terms, use World plus per-country views with sample-size badges and a minimum threshold to hide low-count countries, and group derivates by their prefix letter labeled with sales descriptions.

For the chat feature, I'd recommend a RAG approach with hybrid search over feedback, citing feedback IDs and staying aware of the current page context, implemented via the AI SDK with streaming through a resizable side panel rather than a popup. I'd skip auth entirely in favor of a hardcoded placeholder user, add an engine type filter (ICE/PHEV/BEV/All) next to the region selector since the context calls for per-model and per-engine-type views, and lean on shadcn components for the sidebar, breadcrumbs, and charts.

I'd use static car images in /public with a silhouette fallback since no real assets exist, enhance the analysis landing cards with mini KPIs like feedback count and net sentiment, and persist global filters in URL search params as an implementation detail.

Facts I checked first:

- **Database:** the Neon database has 9,301 feedbacks and 13,035 aspects loaded. 2,561 of the aspects were inferred by the LLM.
- **Cars:** the data only has three derivates: **F70** (1 Series), **G60** (5 Series) and **G70** (7 Series). There's no F60.
- **Geography:** the data has a country code for each feedback but no region field. Coverage is very uneven: US 8.8k rows, GB 2.9k, JP 1.2k, KR 440, and the rest have fewer than 200 each (LV has 3).
- **Missing data:** there's no competitor research or trend research data anywhere, and nothing called "incentives". Feedback has no dates, so nothing in it can show change over time.
- **App:** it's still the bare Next 16 starter. There's no shadcn, no chart library, no chat, no auth and no AI SDK; only the `openai` package is installed.

Round 1:

❓ **Q1** - **Where do competitor and trend research come from?** Nothing in the repo produces either one. Options:
(a) Someone else's pipeline produces it, and the dashboard reads it from a table.
(b) I build a research script (OpenAI web search, one run per derivate and VFC category) that writes findings with source URLs to a `research_findings` table.
(c) Show only customer feedback for now, and leave clearly empty slots for competitor and trend.

➡️ (b), with a deliberately simple schema: `kind` (competitor or trend), `derivate_code`, `country` (empty means global), `vfc_category`, `claim`, `source_title`, `source_url`, `published_at`. That gives every claim a citation, and competitor/trend findings join to feedback through VFC category. If a teammate already owns this data, pick (a) and tell me its shape.

---

❓ **Q2** - **What does "incentives" mean?** The project has no such term. My guess is "how strong the case is for investing in improving this". Options:
(a) **Priority Score** for each aspect, combining how many owners complain, how strongly they complain, and (if Q1 gives us the data) whether competitors do it better or a trend makes it urgent. The car's headline is its overall net sentiment plus its top 3 priorities.
(b) Something else you have in mind, such as cost/benefit or business incentives like sales impact.

➡️ (a). I'll add **Priority Score** to CONTEXT.md once we agree on the formula, which will be a later round.

---

❓ **Q3** - **At what level are aspects prioritised?** You could rank the 16 VFC categories (e.g. "Infotainment & Connectivity") or the much finer aspect terms (e.g. "Touch screen, operation").

➡️ Rank the VFC categories on the first view. Clicking a category drills down to its aspect terms, then its issue types, then the verbatims. Sixteen rows fit on one screen; hundreds of aspect terms don't.

---

❓ **Q4** - **How does the region dropdown work, given we only have countries and the sample is so uneven?**
(a) World plus every country.
(b) World plus only countries with at least N feedbacks (e.g. 30), with the sample size shown everywhere.
(c) Group countries into regions (Europe, North America, APAC).

➡️ (b). Show an "n = 1,158" badge and a low-confidence warning below a threshold. Keep the choice in the URL (`?country=JP`) so a link shows the same view. Without the cutoff, the Latvia view (3 feedbacks) would rank aspects off almost no data. Grouping into regions can come later.

---

❓ **Q5** - **Should there be an engine type filter as well?** CONTEXT.md says the point is to see aspects "per model and engine type", and a BEV owner's pain points differ from an ICE owner's.

➡️ Yes. Add an All / ICE / PHEV / BEV toggle next to the region dropdown, also kept in the URL.

---

❓ **Q6** - **How is the car catalogue grouped?** Your sketch shows G and F series; the data has F70, G60 and G70.

➡️ Build the list from the database and group it by the derivate's first letter, with the sales name on each card ("G60 · BMW 5 Series"). Instead of plain cards, I'd suggest mini scorecards showing feedback count, net sentiment and the #1 priority, so the PM can triage from the catalogue page without opening each car.

---

❓ **Q7** - **What does the chat do?**
(a) Interface only for now.
(b) Answers questions using hybrid search over the feedback data (and the research findings, if Q1 adds them). Every answer cites feedback IDs and source URLs, and the chat knows which car, country and engine type you're currently viewing.

➡️ (b), as a collapsible panel on the right like your sketch, not a popup, so it doesn't cover the charts. This needs adding the `ai` and `@ai-sdk/openai` packages for streaming chat; doing that by hand on the bare `openai` package isn't worth it.

---

❓ **Q8** - **Login and the user block in the sidebar footer?** There's no auth in the app.

➡️ Show a hard-coded placeholder user for now and leave auth out until the dashboard leaves localhost.

---

❓ **Q9** - **UI kit and theme?**

➡️ shadcn/ui: its sidebar, breadcrumb, select, toggle group, sheet and chart components (charts are built on Recharts). Use a dark theme to match your sketches, plus a light theme. Keep it neutral with a single BMW-blue accent, and make the numbers dense rather than decorative.

---

❓ **Q10** - **Where do the car images come from?** There are none in the repo.

➡️ You add one image per derivate to `public/cars/{derivate}.webp`, and any car without one gets a neutral silhouette.
<system-reminder>Note: The user opened the file "/Users/itsmeyaw/projects/bmwow/.codex/hooks.json". This may or may not be relevant to the current task.</system-reminder>

Q2: I mean incentives is the overall user feedback (pos vs neg feedback)
Q7: (a)
Q9: shadcn/ui with light mode. I just added the theme for shadcn using shadcn CLI init
Else: Follow recommendation

For Q4, I'll show every country with no threshold cutoff but keep the n badge visible by default. For the pipeline question, I need to figure out its actual shape rather than assume — since shadcn init was just added, I should check if components.json or related config files reveal the structure.

For incentives, I'm clarifying that it means overall sentiment balance (positive vs negative feedback), both for the car overall and per aspect — though the term "incentive" feels off given CONTEXT.md uses "Sentiment," so I should propose something like "Sentiment Balance" or "Net Sentiment" and confirm whether neutral feedback should count, and whether it's count-based or score-weighted. Prioritization of aspects is a separate concept needing its own formula, to figure out next round.

Chat UI only for Q7, light mode only for Q9 since shadcn is already set up. Before finalizing, I should check components.json, the globals.css theme, and the list of DB tables to confirm these facts.

I'm noting the design should follow the shadcn "base-vega" style with Base UI and hugeicons, using a neutral greyscale palette for charts while reserving green/red for positive/negative values. I'm also thinking through how neutral feedback splits into feature requests versus unclassified items, since feature requests carry real product value, and flagging that competitor/trend data isn't in the database yet which limits what can be shown there.

For now, since the schema for that teammate data is unknown, I'll recommend defining a contract table and showing an empty "No research yet" state until it's populated — also noting the pipeline is still partially loaded at 9,301 of 10,128 records.

On the incentive metric, I'm deciding to count positive versus negative aspects (not feedbacks, since one feedback can hold both), summing aspect counts per car, keeping neutral/"Wants" separate from the ratio, and displaying a Net score scaled -100 to +100 like NPS with a diverging bar, using counts rather than intensity-weighting for clarity. I'm also flagging that "Incentive" as a name is risky since in the auto industry it already means sales/dealer discounts, so a BMW PM would misread it — leaning toward renaming it "Net Sentiment" instead.

For ranking which categories need improvement, I'm leaning toward sorting by raw negative count with intensity as a tiebreaker rather than net ratio alone, since ratio-only would overweight tiny categories, and research/competitor data can't factor in yet since its shape is undefined. I still need to ask the user whether the teammate's research output is keyed by derivative plus VFC category, and whether the "reasoning" shown per category should be an LLM-generated summary or a deterministic template built from counts and top issues.

For citations I'd want verbatim quotes tagged with feedback ID, source, country, and engine type, surfaced through a drill-down sheet sorted by intensity, with a small badge distinguishing curated versus inferred aspects. For the car page layout, I'm sketching a header with region/engine/image and big KPI numbers, followed by a diverging bar chart of the 16 categories as the main visualization, sorted by priority, with row clicks triggering some kind of drill-down since the right panel is reserved for chat.

For the drill-down itself, I'll recommend a dedicated route like /analysis/G60/infotainment with breadcrumbs rather than a sheet, since it's linkable, plus a wants/feature-request panel and maybe a country comparison map when "World" is selected. On color, I'm leaning toward colorblind-safe blue for positive and orange-red for negative instead of green/red, fitting the greyscale theme with a BMW blue accent. For country display, I'll show every country with an n badge rather than filtering, and I'll note the chat backend being unconnected is just a placeholder detail, not something needing a question.

More facts:
- shadcn is set up with the `base-vega` style (built on Base UI, not Radix), Hugeicons and a neutral theme. The chart colours `--chart-1` to `--chart-5` are all **greys**, so positive and negative have no colours yet.
- The database has only `feedback_entries` and `feedback_aspects`. There's no competitor or trend table yet.
- 9,301 of the 10,128 feedbacks are loaded, so the preprocessing run is incomplete or still going.
- Sample, G60 by VFC category as positive / negative / neutral aspects: Infotainment 204/322/87, Powertrain 479/196/52, Access & Keys 47/179/46.

Settled: show every country, chat is interface only, light mode with your shadcn theme, and my recommendations for everything else.

Round 2:

❓ **Q1** - **What does the word "incentive" mean here?** Car-industry PMs already read "incentives" as sales incentives, meaning dealer discounts and lease support. A BMW PM seeing "Incentive: −22" may think of pricing.
(a) Keep "Incentive".
(b) Call it **Net Sentiment** in CONTEXT.md and list "incentive" under avoided terms.

➡️ (b)

---

❓ **Q2** - **How is incentive / net sentiment calculated?**
- Unit: count **aspects** or **feedbacks**? One feedback can contain both praise and a defect.
- Formula: (pos − neg) / (pos + neg) shown as −100 to +100 (like NPS), or just the positive share in %?
- Neutral aspects (feature requests and unclassified): leave them out of the ratio, or count them?

➡️ Count aspects. Use (pos − neg) / (pos + neg) × 100, which works the same for the whole car and for one category. Leave neutral aspects out of the ratio, but show feature requests as their own "Wants" count, because what owners ask for is gold for a PM. Weight by count, not intensity, so a PM can explain it in one sentence.

---

❓ **Q3** - **How do we rank which aspects need improvement?** This is separate from net sentiment.
(a) Most negative aspects first. This favours big problems.
(b) Worst net sentiment first. This lets tiny categories jump to the top: 2 negatives and 0 positives scores −100.
(c) Negative count × average negative intensity. This catches problems that are both big and angry.

➡️ (c). Show the score's parts next to it so the ranking can be audited. Competitor and trend data stay out of the score until their shape is known (Q4); they appear as supporting evidence only.

---

❓ **Q4** - **What will the competitor and trend data look like?** You chose (a), someone else's pipeline, but nothing exists yet. I can either wait for its schema, or define the format their pipeline should write to now and show "No research yet" until data arrives.

➡️ Define the format now: a `research_findings` table with `kind` (competitor or trend), `derivate_code`, `country` (empty means global), `vfc_category`, `claim`, `source_title`, `source_url` and `published_at`, added in `migrations/`. Joining on VFC category puts the research on the same rows as the feedback. If the teammate already has a format, paste it and I'll adapt.

---

❓ **Q5** - **Where does the "reasoning" behind each priority come from?**
(a) Facts generated straight from the data, for example: "322 negatives (18% of G60 negatives), mostly *Usability Difficulty* (140), top aspect term *Touch screen, operation*", followed by the top verbatims as citations.
(b) An LLM-written summary for each category, generated in a batch job and stored.

➡️ (a). It's free, exact and can't hallucinate. (b) can come later if the PM wants prose.

---

❓ **Q6** - **What does a citation look like?**

➡️ A verbatim card showing the Feedback Explorer ID, source, country, engine type and feedback type. For inferred aspects, the quote is highlighted inside the verbatim and the card gets a small "Inferred" badge to distinguish it from human-labelled ones. Strongest verbatims first. Research citations are a title plus a link to the source URL.

---

❓ **Q7** - **Car page layout.** My proposal:
1. **Header:** car image, derivate and sales name, region dropdown, engine type toggle, and n = feedback count.
2. **Overview strip:** a large Net Sentiment number, then positive / negative / wants counts.
3. **Main chart:** a diverging bar chart of all 16 VFC categories, negatives to the left and positives to the right, sorted by priority (Q3). Each row's own net sentiment sits at the row's end. This one chart shows both "net sentiment per aspect" and "what to fix first".
4. **Drill-down:** clicking a row opens a **separate page** `/analysis/G60/infotainment-connectivity`, with the breadcrumb Analysis › G60 › Infotainment. That page shows the aspect term breakdown, the issue types, the reasoning (Q5), the citations (Q6) and the competitor/trend findings.

The drill-down could instead open in a side sheet, but that would collide with the chat panel, and a separate page can be linked to and works with the breadcrumb.

➡️ As proposed.

---

❓ **Q8** - **Which colours for positive and negative?** The theme has none. Options: green/red, the common choice, which red–green colour-blind users can't tell apart; or blue/orange, which is colour-blind-safe and fits a BMW blue accent.

➡️ Blue for positive, orange for negative, grey for neutral, added as `--positive`, `--negative` and `--neutral` variables in `globals.css`.

---

❓ **Q9** - **When showing every country, do we still show the sample size?** Latvia, for example, has 3 feedbacks.

➡️ Yes: put the feedback count in the dropdown ("Latvia · 3") and in the header. No warnings or cutoffs, but the PM can see when there's too little data to trust.
